chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Alaa' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding

a man who says to his slave, 'I free you on the condition that I marry you to my daughter; if you marry (another wife) or take a concubine, one hundred dinars are upon you.' So he frees him on that condition, and he either takes a concubine or marries (another wife). He (peace be upon him) said: 'The condition is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on a slave's freedom when it is granted with a specific financial condition attached?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of 'shart' (stipulation) in conditional manumission, where the master's condition becomes binding upon the freed slave. It highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in allowing specific contractual obligations to persist post-emancipation, provided they do not contradict core legal principles. The ruling underscores the mutual consent and agreed-upon terms that define the master-slave relationship's transition to freedom.
